paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between Loss Ratio and TFLOPs across different models. The x-axis represents TFLOPs on a logarithmic scale, with values ranging from $10^7$ to $9 \cdot 10^8$, and tick labels spaced at irregular intervals. The y-axis represents Loss Ratio as a percentage on a linear scale, with values ranging from 94% to 100%, and tick labels spaced at 1% intervals. The plot displays five lines, each representing a different model: Vanilla (purple, solid, no markers), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid, no markers), SepLLM (n=128) (blue, solid, no markers), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid, no markers), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid, no markers). The Vanilla line remains steady at 99.9% across the x-axis range. The SepLLM (n=64) line starts at approximately 98% at $10^7$ TFLOPs and increases to around 99.7% at $3 \cdot 10^8$ TFLOPs before decreasing to 99.5% at $9 \cdot 10^8$ TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=128) line starts at around 97.2% at $10^7$ TFLOPs and increases to approximately 99.5% at $2 \cdot 10^8$ TFLOPs before remaining steady. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line starts at approximately 98.5% at $10^7$ TFLOPs and increases to around 99.6% at $2 \cdot 10^8$ TFLOPs before decreasing slightly. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line starts at 94% at $10^7$ TFLOPs and increases to around 99% at $3 \cdot 10^8$ TFLOPs before decreasing to 98.5% at $9 \cdot 10^8$ TFLOPs.
